answers.explanation: Hosted mail leaves you with just DNS records and accounts to manage.
It keeps the reputation of bulk mail apart from day-to-day mail.
Public mail should come in through one filtered door: a filtering service or a DMZ relay.
Webmail, ActiveSync, and Outlook on Exchange all ride on HTTPS.
Start at none, read the reports, then tighten to quarantine.
The internal relay never takes mail from outside.
It's an ordinary TXT lookup, so a CNAME to the provider's key works. Only the target of an MX can't be an alias.
The public zone only carries MX, SPF, DKIM, and DMARC. Internal names stay internal.
The MX points at Microsoft. Opening 25 inward would only add risk.
